module.name: ACT Core
module.author: UW DIGI
module.description: The ACT registry's server side: scheduled re-evaluation of every enabled, unretired patient flag, mirrored into patient lists, a look-up of the data missing behind a flag, each patient's prophylaxis adherence and next due date, and loading the report descriptors at startup.

globalProperty.description: The program every newly registered patient is enrolled in, at the session location on the day they are registered. Leave empty to enrol nobody, for example while migrating ACT 2.0 data.

Only flags carrying this tag are mirrored into a patient list. Leave empty to give every enabled flag a list. Useful where some flags are a clinical signal on the chart and are not worth a worklist of their own. A list whose flag loses the tag is kept, emptied.

Name of the cohort type given to lists this module creates. The module creates the type if no cohort type has this name, and creates no lists while a voided type has it. Lists created before this value changes keep their original type.
The obs group, and its member holding the regimen, that records a prophylaxis prescription. The adherence refresh takes the groups of the latest consultation that has any, by its date.
The injection regimens, as regimen answer uuid:days between injections, separated by commas. Any other regimen is treated as oral, whose adherence is the latest estimate.
The member of a prescription group holding the date it started. A prescription without one is left out.
The member of a prescription group holding the date it stopped. A stopped prescription is left out, as ACT 2.0 left it out.
The date an injection was given.
The clinician's oral adherence estimate, in percent. It counts from its encounter's date.
The duration of an oral prescription, recorded with the estimate; it sets when oral prophylaxis is next due.
The prescription duration answers, as answer uuid:days, separated by commas.

The date of a consultation. ACT 2.0 recomputed adherence when a consultation was saved, and its nightly run held a batch-entered patient from the latest consultation or injection until the batch interval passed.
How a patient's injections are entered, recorded on the consultation. As in ACT 2.0 the latest consultation's answer counts, and a consultation that leaves it blank means continuous entry.

The batch data entry answers, as answer uuid:days between batches, separated by commas. ACT 2.0's nightly run skipped such a patient until that long had passed since the later of their latest consultation and injection. Any other answer, such as continuous entry, is recomputed nightly.
